Be careful, however, as a Garrison can be destroyed this way.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]If both a land and a naval unit are stationed in the city, their contributions do not stack; only the unit with the higher [ICON_STRENGTH] Combat Strength contribution applies it, and is the garrison that absorbs incoming damage.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Additional combat units may move through the city, but they cannot end their turn there. If you build a combat unit in a city with a garrison of the same domain, the new unit will be placed adjacent to the city.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]A unit garrisoned in the city may attack surrounding enemy units [COLOR_YELLOW]unless it's a naval unit[ENDCOLOR]

Shopping Mall
The Mall interacts with Corporations and the Trade Route subsystem on which they rely. In an appropriate City, it turns Franchises from a cost into a benefit.

During the 20th century, the advent of the automobile has created an urban and suburban landscape in which people live in one area but can shop, play and work elsewhere - often miles away from their homes. Nowhere is this more true than in the United States of America, whose citizens are noted for an almost fanatical devotion to their cars. This has had important social, environmental and economic affects upon life in America, leading to (among other things) the creation of that most American of institution - the shopping mall.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]American shopping malls are surrounded by acres and acres of parking lots, and they may contain dozens (if not hundreds) of stores selling everything from clothing to jewelry to electronics to books to computers to videos. In some ways American shopping malls are akin in spirit to the old Arabian markets (although Americans don't particularly enjoy haggling and prices are generally fixed).[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The earliest automobile-centered shopping center was the "Market Square," opened in Chicago, Illinois, in 1916. Constructed in Minnesota in 1992, the "Mall of America" is the largest mall in the world at time of writing. It contains over 500 shops, 80 restaurants, a theme park, hotel, and movie theatres. It is housed in a building large enough to hold over 30 Boeing 747 airplanes.
World Trade Center

[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"The World Trade Center is a living symbol of man's dedication to world peace... a representation of man's belief in humanity, his need for individual dignity, his beliefs in the cooperation of men, and, through cooperation, his ability to find greatness." [NEWLINE]- Minoru Yamasaki[NEWLINE][TAB]

The World Trade Center was a complex of buildings in New York City, that are currently being replaced with new structures after the original was destroyed. The original World Trade Center featured landmark twin towers, which opened on April 4, 1973, and were destroyed in the September 11th terrorist attacks of 2001, along with 7 World Trade Center. The original World Trade Center was thought of as a North American cultural icon, and at the time of their completion, the "Twin Towers", the original 1 World Trade Center (the North Tower), at 417 metres (1,368 ft), and 2 World Trade Center (the South Tower), were the tallest buildings in the world.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]On the morning of September 11, 2001, Al-Qaeda-affiliated hijackers flew two Boeing 767 jets into the complex, one into each tower, in a coordinated act of terrorism. After burning for 56 minutes, the South Tower collapsed, followed a half-hour later by the North Tower. The attacks on the World Trade Center killed 2,753 people. Falling debris from the towers, combined with fires that the debris initiated in several surrounding buildings, led to the partial or complete collapse of all the other buildings in the complex and caused catastrophic damage to ten other large structures in the surrounding area (including the World Financial Center). content.text: The Hwacha, legendary Korean anti-infantry weapon, was a unique innovation in the development of early gunpowder-based weaponry. Created during the 15th century under the supervision of King Sejong the Great, the Hwacha consisted of a large two-wheeled cart carrying a type of "honeycomb" housing, not unlike a modern missile battery, capable of storing hundreds of gunpowder-propelled arrows. The light-weight of these early rockets, known as "Singijeon," provided the Hwacha with a notable advantage, allowing excellent maneuverability compared to a traditional cannon. The Hwacha would prove to be a formidable weapon for the defense of the Korean Peninsula during the Japanese invasions of the 16th century.

content.text: Tophet

"Tophet" is a Hebrew term for a place of worship and human sacrifice to the Canaanite gods, and has become a colorful synonym for hell within Judeo-Christian theology. Usually located outside cities, Tophets were holy places where sacrifices could be presented to gods of the Phoenician pantheon.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Regular sacrifices were made to ensure the prosperity of Carthage and the ashes of burnt offerings were sealed within the Tophet. Child sacrifice, once prevalent throughout the Near-East, was a persistent hallmark of Carthaginian religious life long after contemporary cultures had shunned the practice. Modern archaeological evidence suggests children were sacrificed in times of great stress such as wars, plagues, and natural disasters as an act of divine supplication.

The Tophet is the unique Shrine replacement for Carthage. In addition to the normal bonuses of a Shrine, the Tophet provides Culture whenever Gold is spent in the City. Therefore, you want to avoid spending your early Gold in a City before it has a Tophet constructed. In effect, the value of Gold and Faith are increased by a percentage, increasing their value from all sources. Helpfully, the Tophet also provides a steady trickle of Gold, allowing more purchases throughout the game.
Mikasa

The Mikasa represents the pinnacle of pre-dreadnought battleship design and serves as a symbol of Japan's rapid industrialization and emergence as a global naval power. Built in the United Kingdom by Vickers for the Imperial Japanese Navy, she was commissioned in 1902 and named after Mount Mikasa in Nara.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]At the time of her launch, the Mikasa was the most advanced battleship in the world, featuring a formidable primary armament of four 12-inch guns and Krupp cemented armor that provided superior protection. Her design focused on a balance of speed, firepower, and resilience that would soon be tested in one of history's most decisive naval engagements.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The ship earned its place in legend during the Russo-Japanese War (1904-1905). As the flagship of Admiral Togo Heihachiro, the Mikasa led the Japanese fleet during the Battle of Tsushima. Despite taking multiple direct hits, she remained operational, coordinating the maneuver that effectively annihilated the Russian Baltic Fleet. This victory was a watershed moment, marking the first time in modern history that an Asian power defeated a European power in a major naval war.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Though the dreadnought revolution made pre-dreadnoughts like the Mikasa technically obsolete shortly after the war, her cultural impact remained immense. Today, she is preserved as a museum ship in Yokosuka, standing as the last remaining example of a pre-dreadnought battleship in the world and a monument to Japan's maritime heritage.

This provides Morocco with a bit of pathway to pursuing a Cultural Victory as the rest of their kit is fairly well rounded.

The Corsair has the Razzia promotion so it gains [ICON_FOOD] Food and [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production on kills, pillaging Improvements, and plundering [ICON_INTERNATIONAL_TRADE] Trade Routes. This synergizes well with their unique ability to plunder [ICON_INTERNATIONAL_TRADE] Trade Routes without declaring war. Morocco should look for opportunities to be aggressive against other civs that have weaker navies especially those with plenty of sea Improvements that they could pillage.

Compared to the Cannon, the Great Bombard has very high [ICON_RANGE_STRENGTH] Ranged Combat Strength, a larger bonus against Cities, and a larger penalty against Units. This makes it a glass cannon which is incredible at doing damage to Cities but vulnerable to melee attackers with its fairly low [ICON_STRENGTH] Combat Strength. A Charbagh is a walled garden divided into four square sections that is distinctive to Indo-Persian culture. These gardens trace their roots to the pairidaeza of the Achaemenid empire, and perhaps back even further to Assyrian garden designs. Persian and later Persianized cultures employed garden building as a subtle way to demonstrate the King of King's command over his realm and the natural world within it through the creation of public spaces.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The Persian gardens have captured the imaginations of Mediterranean and western thinkers. The pairidaeza is the root of the Greek "paradise", informing modern notions of an earthly Eden in art and poetry.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The Charbagh can be built by [ICON_WORKER] Workers on Land with access to Fresh Water, and not next to another Charbagh.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Each Charbagh yields [ICON_FOOD] Food, [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production, [ICON_GOLD] Gold, and [ICON_CULTURE] Culture. content.text: The Qizilbash provides yields on pillage including [ICON_GOLDEN_AGE] Golden Age Points and can always be [ICON_PEACE] Faith purchased. This combines well with Persia's existing bonuses for aggressive expansion and [ICON_GOLDEN_AGE] Golden Ages.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Ensuring you have a strong [ICON_PEACE] Faith income once you unlock the Qizilbash can help to quickly purchase a number of them and replace them when any of them get killed. Once you have a good number of Qizilbash, you'll want to look for opportunities to fight aggressive wars where you can pillage as many tiles as possible. A good way to approach this is to target any weaker neighbors.

The Barbican provides a free Castle, +1 Military Supply, and City defense bonuses. It costs 50% more [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production so essentially absorbs half the Castle [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production cost.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]With the extra Military Supply and free Castle, it provides quite an increase in Military Supply that pushes Poland towards more of a military focus. This allows them to build lots of their Unique Units and look for opportunities to expand at the expense of their neighbors.

The Pancerny has bonus defense and bonus attack against Wounded Units and Units in Open Terrain. Before Tercios arrive, it can be used more aggressively than other Skirmisher Units and can often be left along the frontlines.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The attack bonuses increase its potential damage and help finish off Wounded Units. It's still best paired with Mounted Units like Knights to take advantage of its flanking bonus from Skirmisher Doctrine.

Caçadores gain +1 [ICON_MOVES] Movement and become stronger as they lose HP. Their mobility makes them excellent for advancing through rough terrain, since they can move onto Hills and still fire in the same turn. Before Landships arrive, they can be effective on the front line as they are more durable and hit harder while wounded as well as being able to quickly reposition when heavily damaged.

The University of Coimbra provides the Age of Discovery promotion to all units generating [ICON_GOLD] Gold and Experience as they reveal tiles. It unlocks just before Naus which are often the best unit to use to then explore the world.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production bonus for [ICON_TRADE] Trade Units allows any City to very quickly replace any lost [ICON_TRADE] Trade Units to keep their unique ability yields flowing.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]It also provides a free University in the City and gives all Universities bonus [ICON_GOLD] Gold which you should often prioritize building.

The Pogost provides extra yields on Villages/Towns and it receives additional yields every Technology level for the next 2 eras.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]This often makes building Villages worthwhile even outside of [ICON_CONNECTED] City Connections. Therefore, you should consider prioritizing any bonuses to Villages, since you'll then have lots of them.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Additionally, it's often worth prioritizing the Technologies that provide bonus yields to Pogosts, especially Industrialization as it provides the largest bonus.

The Licorne has an attack bonus against Melee/Gunpowder units and the ability to move after attacking. This essentially allows it to function as both a Siege and Ranged unit. Being able to move after attacking provides a lot of flexibility when advancing so it can look to position to fire every turn. It also helps when retreating so it can fire before moving back to safety.

Buffalo Pounds provide bonus yields for each tile owned by the City which synergizes well with Shoshone's unique ability. Prioritizing anything that provides border growth so Cities can expand more frequently can help to maximize the yields that it provides.

Yellow Brows are defensive-oriented units which receive bonus Combat Strength when fortified and become stronger as they take damage. This allows them to be more durable and often stay fortified on the front lines longer because their Combat Strength increases as they become damaged unlike regular units.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]If you use ranged and mounted units to deal most of the damage then Yellow Brows can stay fortified so they can absorb more enemy attacks and heal.

Gumeys provide bonus yields when a [ICON_INTERNATIONAL_TRADE] Trade Route passes through the City that it's built in similar to how Villages/Towns receive bonus yields from passing [ICON_INTERNATIONAL_TRADE] Trade Routes. They also give bonus [ICON_INTERNATIONAL_TRADE] Land Trade Route range and additional [ICON_GOLD] Gold on [ICON_INTERNATIONAL_TRADE] International Trade Routes.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]To take advantage of this, you want to try to setup long [ICON_INTERNATIONAL_TRADE] Trade Routes that pass through as many of your Cities as possible so they can each receive the bonus yields.

Sofas unlock around the same time as Mandekalu Cavalry and together they provide a very strong military power spike for Songhai to go on the offensive. While Mandekalu Cavalry are the workhorse units, Sofas provide additional healing through having the Medic I promotion and have bonus Combat Strength against Mounted Units which minimizes one of their only counters.

Fusta are to Venice as the Galleass is to other Civilizations, and Venetian Liburna upgrade to the Fusta rather than the Great Galleass. A fief usually took the form of revenue-producing lands which the noble could levy taxes from, in which case the estate was called a Fiefdom, but it could also take other forms, such as a trade monopoly or resource rights, like mining. These fiefs were central to the Medieval feudal system, and allowed kings to bind knights to their service without the need for the large bureaucracies and costs of a standing army; it was up to knights to sustain their own livelihoods once they had been given the means to do so.

According to this doctrine, only God can judge an unjust king. content.text: A subsidy is any financial aid provided by a government to a producer or seller of a good or service that is designed to increase the competitiveness of a particular industry firm or entire industry. An employment subsidy can protect jobs in a crisis, a transport subsidy can open up new transport routes, and an export subsidy can be used to pursue a policy of mercantilism.
content.oldText: Free trade is a policy followed by some international markets in which governments do not restrict imports from or exports to other countries. Free trade is exemplified by the European Economic Area and the North American Free Trade Agreement, which have established open markets. Most nations are today members of the World Trade Organization (WTO) multilateral trade agreements. However, most governments still impose some protectionist policies that are intended to support local employment, such as applying tariffs to imports or subsidies to exports. Governments may also restrict free trade to limit exports of natural resources. Other barriers that may hinder trade include import quotas, taxes, and non-tariff barriers, such as regulatory legislation.

content.text: Throughout history, precious metals have formed the basis of (commodity) money. As large sums became traded more commonly, representative money in the form of notes and certificates became the main medium of exchange. In this context, a gold standard is a monetary system in which representative money is exchangable for a fixed quantity of gold bullion. This was done to maintain stable exchange rates and limit inflation, although these effects are not guaranteed and the choice comes with significant monetary policy implications. The gold standard was the basis for the international monetary system from the 1870s to the early 1920s, and intermittently until 1971 when the world's reserve currency, the US dollar, terminated its convertibility policy.

content.oldText: The Age of Enlightenment (or simply the Enlightenment or Age of Reason) is the time period in which cultural and social changes occurred emphasizing reason, analysis and individualism rather than traditional ways of thinking. Initiated by philosophes beginning in late 17th-century Western Europe the process of change fueled from voluntary organizations of men who were committed to the betterment of society. These men convened at coffeehouses, salons and masonic lodges. Institutions that were deeply rooted in society, such as religion and the government began to be questioned and a greater emphasis was placed on ways to reform society with toleration, science and skepticism.

content.text: Philosopher John Locke is often credited with founding liberalism as a distinct tradition based on the social contract, arguing that each man has a natural right to life, liberty and property, and governments must not violate these rights. From the Glorious Revolution of 1688, through the American Revolution and French Revolutions of late 1700s, to the Tanzimat reform of the Ottoman empire beginning in 1839, liberal philosophy was used to justify the armed overthrow of royal sovereignty and the rise of consitutionalism.
content.oldText: A scientific revolution is a period when rapid advances in human knowledge or technology overturns the current worldview, as a result triggering yet more advancements in thought and knowledge. Much of Europe underwent a scientific revolution in the 16th century, following the publication of Nicolaus Copernicus' work, "On the Revolutions of the Heavenly Spheres" and Andreas Vesalius' "On the Fabric of the Human Body In Seven Books." Both used modern (for the period) scientific practices to examine parts of the world around them and overturned incorrect scientific theories, some dating back to the ancient Greeks. Following the success of these books, the floodgates were opened, and scientists began carefully examining everything around them, and human knowledge increased exponentially over the succeeding centuries.
